outcome.technical: run-test-gate.py now reads every runner output through _runner_output.plain_text(): _named_failures, _suite_candidates, reached_a_verdict, _named_failure_count, _stopped_early, _other_failures and mute_ineligible each normalise their text on entry, and playwright_listed reads plain_text(text).splitlines(). The private copy `_CSI = re.compile(_CSI_TEXT)` is deleted (it repeated what plain_text already strips), and so are the _ANSI.sub calls plain_text makes redundant. The _ro aliases ro1 pins (_CSI_TEXT, _ANSI, ...) stay. The CRLF bugs this fixes go beyond failing names: TAP's closing tallies (reached_a_verdict), vitest's --bail `Test Files` count (_stopped_early, which would have let a mute excuse a bailed run on Windows) and jest's `Summary of all failing tests` split (_named_failure_count, which refused a valid mute on Windows). New lint in tools/lints/_output_lints.py: runner_line_end_violations(dirs=None, home='_runner_output', pending=None) plus RUNNER_LINE_END_PENDING. Its scope is _runner_output itself and every module under scripts/ that imports it. It finds a search/match/fullmatch/findall/finditer/sub/subn/split call on a pattern compiled re.M/re.MULTILINE/(?m) with an unescaped `$` outside a character class. The pattern can be the module's own, borrowed by name or attribute, a table entry read by key or .get, a table looped over, or a local bound to one. The call is reported when its text argument is not shown line-end-free within the function. The docstring says what it cannot see. RUNNER_LINE_END_PENDING holds three debt rows in files this task does not own: _runner_output._pytest_cases and _runner_output._pytest_tally (both take text failing_cases and read_tally already normalised) and stamp-verification.final_error (it .strip()s its capture). A row whose site goes quiet is reported. Tests: sf12 and sf13 in tests/test_run_test_gate.py (in _suite_files_cases), and le1-le4 in tests/test__output_lints.py (new _line_end_cases). Gate `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_run_test_gate.py tests/test__output_lints.py` exited 1. test_run_test_gate.py ok (571 cases). test__output_lints.py printed SELFTEST FAILED 171/173. The only failures are te11 and ln1, and both name tests/test__runner_output.py:469, a file I did not touch: L.truncated_evidence_violations() returns the same finding on a pristine `git archive HEAD` export, so it was red before this task. le1-le4 PASS. ruff check on the 4 files: exit 0. vermin -t=3.8-: exit 0. NOT DONE, plan gate refused: the prove-gates rows. An Edit of tools/prove-gates.py was refused verbatim with: `[require-plan] tools/prove-gates.py is outside task P142.13-6yq, the task this worktree is bound to ... Only that task's files are open here.` Without the rows, prove-gates' own c1 (coverage()) and its allow_coverage() report runner_line_end_violations as missing (measured: coverage() == ['reach_graph', 'runner_line_end_violations']; reach_graph is a pre-existing gap from tools/affected.py). The intended rows were each proven in a full copy of plugins/, tools/ and tests/ in scratch, with mutate, run le cases, discard; the worktree was untouched. RED cripple (`return []` after the def line) turns le1 red. RED real-tree (reached_a_verdict's `body = _ro.plain_text(text)` changed back to `body = text or ""`) turns le4 red. ALLOW scope widened (drop the import-scope `continue`) turns le2 red. ALLOW plain_text no longer vouches (`in (RUNNER_TEXT_NORMALISER, "splitlines")` changed to `in ()`) turns le2 red. ALLOW pending ignored (`if site not in pending:` changed to `if True:`) turns le3 red. The exact row text is in the hand-back report.
outcome.descriptive: The gate reads every test run's output through the one CRLF/escape normalisation, so Windows line ends no longer leak into failing names or flip TAP, vitest-bail and jest-summary verdicts; a new lint reports the next private reader that skips it.
